chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The snake, the treacherous black one, and every evil snake, and the scorpion, and the mouse (which is the small rat), can be killed in the Haram (sanctuary) and in Ihram (state of pilgrimage consecration). The crow and the buzzard are to be pelted (with stones). So if thieves present themselves to you, defend yourself from them.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What animals can be killed in Ihram according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific fauna permissible to kill during Ihram, distinguishing between creatures like snakes and scorpions that are killed outright and birds like crows and buzzards that are stoned (rajman). It further extends the ruling to include protection against thieves (lususun) within the sacred precincts, reflecting the broader Shia jurisprudential emphasis on preserving the sanctity of the Haram from both physical impurities and human threats.
